title: Dock Threshold
statement: A harbor lists dock capacities in nondecreasing order. Return the zero-based index of the first dock whose capacity is at least load. If every dock is too small, or the list is empty, return -1. Several docks may have the same capacity; choose the earliest qualifying index.
constraints: capacities is sorted in nondecreasing order.

examples.explanation: Both indices 1 and 2 have capacity 5, but index 1 is the first qualifying dock.
No capacity reaches the required load.

hints.content: The answer divides docks that are too small from docks that qualify.
Because capacities are sorted, that boundary never moves backward.
Binary search can locate the first true position of the condition capacity >= load.
Keep a half-open search interval. When the middle qualifies, retain its left half including the middle.
Start left at zero and right at the array length. Stop when they meet; return -1 if that position is past the final dock.

testCases.explanation: Both indices 1 and 2 have capacity 5, but index 1 is the first qualifying dock.
No capacity reaches the required load.

solutions.title: Inspect docks in order
solutions.intuition: Scanning left to right naturally finds the earliest qualifying dock.
solutions.approach: Return the first index whose capacity is at least the load. If the scan ends, return -1.
solutions.pseudocode: For each index in order: if capacity >= load return index; return -1.
commonMistakes: Returning immediately on equality may select a later duplicate.
When the midpoint fails, advance to mid + 1 so the search always shrinks.
solutions.interviewExplanation: This is a search for the first qualifying position, not any matching value. I keep a half-open interval around the boundary and discard half of it at every comparison. Equal values remain on the qualifying side, which preserves the first-index requirement.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: After exploring every allowed candidate, return the best valid result under the statement’s rules.

solutions.title: Find the qualifying boundary
solutions.intuition: Sorted data lets each comparison discard a region that cannot contain the first qualifying dock.
solutions.approach: Maintain [left,right). If the midpoint qualifies, move right to mid. Otherwise move left to mid + 1. At convergence, check whether the index exists.
solutions.pseudocode: left = 0; right = n; while left < right: mid = left + floor((right-left)/2); if capacities[mid] >= load: right = mid; else: left = mid+1.
commonMistakes: Returning immediately on equality may select a later duplicate.
When the midpoint fails, advance to mid + 1 so the search always shrinks.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: For [2,5,5,9] and load 5, the first midpoint is index 2. It qualifies, so move right to 2.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Index 1 also qualifies, so move right to 1. Index 0 is too small, so move left to 1.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: The bounds meet at index 1, which is the first qualifying dock.
